    <h2>Independent, atmosphere-based estimates of UK greenhouse gas emissions</h2>
    <p>GEMMA combines measurements from atmospheric monitoring stations across the
    UK and Ireland with inverse modelling to produce independent estimates of
    greenhouse gas emissions from each part of the country — providing an evidence
    base that is separate from the statistical methods used in official greenhouse
    gas inventories.</p>
  </div>

     wrapper divs needed. -->

## About the project {.section-header .column-screen}

GEMMA (Greenhouse gas Emissions Measurement and Modelling Advancement) is a UK
research collaboration of nine organisations, led by the National Physical
Laboratory and funded by UKRI from April 2023 to March 2027. It develops ways to
check the UK's reported greenhouse gas emissions against what is measured in the
atmosphere.

GEMMA has added instruments to the UK's atmospheric monitoring network, supported
a new ten-station network that measures carbon dioxide and methane using sunlight,
and improved the inverse models that turn these measurements into emissions
estimates. The aim is a system that can report UK emissions month by month, as an
independent check on the national greenhouse gas inventory.

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 1.75rem;"}
[Read more about GEMMA](about.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
:::
